name: Embraer ERJ 135/140/145
summary: Slender 37–50-seat regional jet family flown in the US by CommuteAir for United, JSX and Contour.

wings: Plain tips on most; small winglets on the ERJ145XR
engines: Two Rolls-Royce AE3007 turbofans in pods high on the rear fuselage, well behind the wing
fuselage: Small round windows; ERJ135 is noticeably shorter
tail: Small ventral strakes under the rear fuselage on some versions

tellTales: Pencil-thin fuselage with rear engines and a T-tail
Engines mounted far aft, well behind the wing

confusedWith.howToTell: The ERJ145 is slimmer (3-abreast) with a longer pointed nose and engines set further aft; the CRJ200 is fatter with winglets and engines close behind the wing.
The ERJ145 has rear engines and a T-tail on a very thin body; the E175 has underwing engines and a low tail.
The ERJ145 is far longer with a row of many small airline windows; the Praetor/Legacy 500 is a short business jet with a few large windows.
